summary: A user listing reports an apparent fire tower above the Murray Mine site in Greater Sudbury; no agency source confirms it, and the site is private.

facts.status_note: Only a user-written listing says a structure that appears to be a firetower stands on the site.

access.note: The listing says the mine is on private property belonging to INCO, with no directions given. The Ontario record says part of the site is in an active mine complex and was not inspected.

evidence.supports: Murray Mine listed in Greater Sudbury, Ontario
evidence.quote: Murray Mine - Greater Sudbury, Ontario - Ominous

evidence.supports: A structure that appears to be a firetower watches over the site
evidence.quote: What appears to be a firetower watches over the site.

evidence.supports: The mine is near Copper Cliff

notes_for_editor: The brief has the kind and status as unknown. The only tower mention is a user listing that says 'what appears to be a firetower' and an unsourced reader comment; no agency, survey or Lands and Forests source was found. The 1963 Lands and Forests tower map, cited on forestrangers.github.io, would show whether a tower was listed here; it was not fetched. Mine dates conflict or are missing: the listing gives a February 1884 first claim and an opening that year, while the Ontario record gives a closing date but no opening date. The listing calls the site abandoned; the Ontario record says it is part of an active complex. Access is private; do not present the site as visitable. The brief's coordinates (46.51168, -81.0635) look close to the Ontario record's UTM point (zone 17, 494870 E, 5151053 N) on a rough conversion, not checked.
